summary: DAY 137 UPDATE (July 7–14): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED JUL 7. CENTCOM ran five-plus strike waves in seven days — 300+ targets across the first three nights, ~170 over Jul 8–9, ~140 on Jul 12, further waves Jul 13–14 — hitting air-defense systems, coastal radar, missile/drone sites, naval capabilities and IRGC small boats along Iran's southern coast. First combat use of one-way attack sea drones (Saronic Corsair USV) at Bandar Abbas Naval Base (Jul 12). Trigger: Iran fired on 3 Hormuz-area tankers Jul 7 (a 'gross violation' of the June 17 MOU per the US); Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' Jul 8 and revoked the Iranian oil-sales license; the US naval blockade of Iranian ports was REIMPOSED effective Jul 14, 20:00 GMT. PRIOR — DAY 129 UPDATE (July 1–6): The June 29 stand-down held for the entire window — ZERO new US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory or maritime traffic July 1–6, corroborated by GlobalSecurity.org's Day 125 report ('no new US offensive action against Iran reported') and the daily update calendar through Day 128 (July 5). Combat froze while diplomacy advanced: indirect US–Iran technical talks in Doha (July 1–2, via Qatari and Pakistani mediators) concluded with 'positive progress' (Qatar FM spokesman Majed al-Ansari, July 2), agreeing a mechanism to use part of the $6B in frozen, Qatar-held Iranian funds for goods purchases and a violations-communications channel; Hormuz tolls, asset-transfer specifics, nuclear inspections and Lebanon remain unresolved. Talks are set to resume ~July 11 after Ayatollah Khamenei's multi-day state funeral (July 4–9; main Tehran procession July 6). The last US kinetic action on Iran remains the June 26–27 Hormuz-area strikes. PRIOR (Day 123): First US kinetic strikes on Iranian territory since the June 17 MOU: 14 targets across June 26–27 (June 26: 4 targets/6 aircraft near Sirik; June 27: 10 targets in and near the Strait of Hormuz), followed by a 'stand-down for now' June 28–29. The re-escalation traced to the Hormuz shipping dispute — IRGC drone attacks on M/V Ever Lovely (Jun 25) and M/T Kiku (Jun 27) over which route ships use (US/JMIC's widened Omani-coast corridor vs Iran's IRGC-designated route near the Iranian coast). Iranian/IRGC reporting cited infrastructure damage only (Sirik telecom tower + 2 water reservoirs); no new casualty figures published. The MOU survived but Axios called it 'barely 11 days old and already on shaky ground.' Nuclear sites (Natanz/Esfahan/Fordow) assessed largely destroyed with little significant activity since the war; ~440kg of 60% HEU slated for on-site downblending under IAEA per the MOU. Doha talks announced for June 30 (Iran unconfirmed).

DAY 86 UPDATE: No US or Israeli kinetic strikes on Iranian territory May 23–24. CENTCOM issued no new strike releases. Trump on Truth Social Saturday May 23 ~17:00 ET: 'An Agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries… Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly' — characterized as a 'Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE.' Trump REVERSED tone Sunday May 24: 'I have informed my representatives not to rush into a deal in that time is on our side. The Blockade will remain in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed.' Senior US administration official to NBC News: 'The Iran agreement will not be signed today, but there has been progress on a deal'; separate US official told Axios deal is '95% there' with negotiators 'haggling over language' on Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and Hormuz arrangements. Iran FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei (state TV / IRIB / IRNA): the framework is a 14-clause MoU providing a 30-60-day window for follow-on negotiations covering ending the war on all fronts (incl. Lebanon), the Strait of Hormuz, the US naval blockade ('US maritime piracy'), release of frozen Iranian assets, and sanctions relief — nuclear program explicitly NOT in the initial MoU but deferred. President Masoud Pezeshkian: 'We are ready to assure the world that we are not seeking nuclear weapons. We are not seeking instability in the region.' PM Netanyahu (X / Israeli statement May 24): 'any final agreement with Iran must eliminate the nuclear threat entirely. This means dismantling Iran's uranium enrichment facilities and removing enriched nuclear material from its territory… Iran will never have a bomb.' IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir approved operational plans for 'continued combat in the Northern Command region on the border with Lebanon'; IDF said it 'is prepared to resume intense combat operations immediately and to further weaken the Iranian terror regime.' Netanyahu convened an emergency cabinet meeting Sunday night amid Israeli alarm at deal terms; Channel 12 reported senior security officials view the emerging deal as not serving Israel's interest. CENTCOM (May 23 press release): cumulative blockade now 100 commercial vessels redirected, 4 disabled, 26 humanitarian aid ships permitted through since Apr 13 blockade began — 'more than 15,000 service members and 200+ aircraft and warships' anchored by two CSGs (Lincoln + Bush) plus a Marine Expeditionary Unit. Iran's Mehr News Agency (May 24) claimed Iranian army air defenses shot down an Israeli-made 'Orbiter' surveillance UAV over Hormozgan province and recovered the wreckage with Iranian naval help — IDF said it was 'NOT FAMILIAR with the incident.' UNVERIFIED single-sourced Iranian claim. DAY 84 UPDATE: No US or Israeli strikes executed on May 22; CENTCOM and Department of War issued no strike releases on Iranian territory. Al Jazeera Day-84 live blog and summary report no new US/Israeli kinetic action against Iran proper. Trump (Oval Office May 21): 'We're going to either make sure they don't have a nuclear weapon, or we're going to have to do something very drastic… we'll probably destroy [the enriched uranium] after we get it, but we're not going to let them have it.' SecState Rubio: 'some good signs' from negotiations and 'some progress' while Washington retains 'other options.' Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir landed in Tehran with high-level security delegation and was received by Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni; Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi continued meetings with Iranian FM Araghchi to deliberate draft agreements ending the war. Qatar assumed a secondary mediator role same day despite suffering the wartime Iranian strike on Ras Laffan LNG. Atlantic Council tracker (May 15 baseline) notes US has expended >1,000 JASSMs, >1,000 Tomahawks, ~1,000 Patriot interceptors, ~45% of Precision Strike Missile stockpile and ~50% of THAAD interceptors. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told the Senate the $14B Taiwan arms sale is PAUSED to preserve munitions for the Iran campaign. Iranian MP Fadahossein Maleki (state TV): 'It could even come from Iran's side, frankly. If we feel that something is happening from a US base, Iran has the legitimacy to respond and prevent it' — flagged as rhetoric, not action. DAY 83 UPDATE: No US or Israeli strikes executed on May 20–21; the postponed May 19 operation never ran. Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews May 20 he was 'an hour away from making the decision to go today' before standing down at the request of Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE; on May 21 he reiterated he was 'willing to wait a few more days' to 'get the right answers' from Tehran. Israel's army Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said the IDF remained 'on the highest level of alert and prepared for any development,' but launched no strike on Iran May 20–21. Operation Epic Fury remains 'concluded' per Sec. Rubio (May 6); the threat-of-resumption posture is now the dominant signal. DAY 82 UPDATE: Trump's postponement held through May 20 (Day 82). Trump told Coast Guard Academy graduates in New London, CT the U.S. is 'in no hurry' but 'we may have to hit them even harder. But maybe not.' No U.S. strikes executed; the postponed operation never ran. Iran's public posture HARDENED: FM Araghchi posted that a 'return to war will feature many more surprises'; the IRGC (May 20, via Sepah News) issued an explicit threat that renewed aggression would spread the war 'beyond the region' with 'crushing blows… in places you cannot even imagine.' CENTCOM blockade tally rose to 91 vessels redirected (4 disabled); 31st MEU Marines boarded the Iranian-flagged M/T Celestial Sea in the Gulf of Oman May 19. DAY 81 UPDATE: Trump told reporters at the White House May 19 he had been 'all set to go' — 'It would have been happening right now' — confirming the Tuesday strike was 'an hour away' from execution before postponement at the personal request of Tamim/MBS/MBZ. Trump publicly framed the postponement as 'two or three days' (Al Jazeera). NSC convened in Situation Room May 19 (Axios). DAY 80 UPDATE: Trump publicly disclosed AND postponed a 'scheduled attack of Iran tomorrow' (Tue May 19) via Truth Social May 18 after MBS, MBZ, and Qatari Emir Tamim asked him to 'hold off' citing 'serious negotiations'; first public disclosure of any imminent strike package since April 8 ceasefire (no CENTCOM or independent corroboration that package was actually being prepared — UNVERIFIED per CBS News). Trump told Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chair Caine to 'be prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice.' May 8 Sea Star III/Sevda disablements remain most recent kinetic action; Day 79 marks 40 days since last Iranian territorial strike Apr 7. DAY 79 ESCALATION RISK SPIKE: Drone strike on UAE Barakah Nuclear Plant (Al Dhafra) Sun May 17 — fire at electrical generator outside inner perimeter, Unit 3 on emergency diesel, no radiological release, no casualties; attribution UNVERIFIED, suspicion on Iran or Iraq-based Shia militia; Saudi Arabia separately intercepted three drones from Iraqi airspace. Trump Truth Social May 17: 'For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them. TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!' Axios/Ravid (May 17): Trump to convene Situation Room Tue May 19 to review military options; AP cites Israeli officer that Israel is 'coordinating with the U.S. about a possible resumption of attacks'; Netanyahu (May 17 cabinet): 'we are prepared for any scenario.' IRGC spokesperson Zolfaghari: U.S. Persian Gulf bases will be 'deactivated.' Posture: HEIGHTENED rhetorical escalation, no kinetic order yet. NYT (May 15): US-Israel 'intensifying preparations for potential attacks on Iran, possibly starting as soon as next week' incl. possible commando raid to retrieve nuclear material + resumed Kharg Island strikes (UNVERIFIED planning leak). Wikipedia (May 16): Trump admin reportedly told UAE to seize Kharg — UNVERIFIED. Project Freedom remains PAUSED-BUT-CLEARED — no restart announcement from Pentagon May 13-16; Hegseth May 12 House Approps line that ceasefire 'remains in effect despite recent exchanges of fire' carries forward. Seven-day pause spans Trump-Xi Beijing summit (Days 76-77); summit closed May 15 with no joint statement but Xi reportedly pledged no military equipment to Iran (per Trump to Hannity) and both sides agreed strait must remain open. Aboard Air Force One returning from Beijing May 15, Trump told reporters he is 'losing patience' with Iran and warned of 'cleanup work' / 'annihilation' absent acceptance of his 14-point framework — but paired this with a reported '20-year moratorium' offer per Open Source Intel video / HotAir; primary text UNCONFIRMED. Posture: rhetorical escalation, no operational order.)
